WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR) In this petition, petitioner seeks for the following reliefs:-
" i. Quash the endorsement dated: 26.12.2018 issued by respondent no. 2 in the file no. KHB/LA/RAICHUR/01/2018- 19, the certified copy of which is at Annexure-G. ii.
Issue any other writ or direction as this Hon'ble court deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the case."
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.
3.

A perusal of the material record will indicate that the subject land bearing Sy.No.99/4 situated at Manavi Taluk, Raichur District, owned and possessed by the petitioner was acquired by the respondents and an award came to be vide Annexure-C dated NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 31.03.2017.

It is the specific contention of the petitioner that no notice of the award was issued or served upon the petitioner, who could not seek a reference before the 2nd respondent-SLAO in terms of Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the said Act of 2013').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
However, the petitioner submitted a representation to the 2nd respondent - SLAO within the extendable / condonable period of one year on 26.09.2018 since the said period of one year as contemplated under the second proviso as contemplated under the second proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 64 of the said Act of 2013 Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176140793/
2 would expire only on 31.09.2018 and consequently, the said representation was within the said period.

4. It is the grievance of the petitioner that it was only when the 3rd respondent initiated proceedings under Section 77(1) of the said Act of 2013 that the petitioner came to know about the said proceedings and the impugned Endorsement issued by the 2nd respondent rejecting the claim of the petitioner on the ground that it was barred by limitation, is contrary to facts and law warranting interference by this Court in the present petition.

In support of his NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 contentions, learned counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon the order of this Court in the case of Smt.Pushpa vs. State of Karnataka and others - W.P.No.216421/2020 dated 12.06.2024 in relation to the lands situated in the same village arising out of the same Notification and acquisition proceedings.

entities.text: Smt.Pushpa vs. State of Karnataka and others - W.P.No.216421/2020 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was therefore submitted that the impugned Endorsement deserves to be quashed and the present petition deserves to be allowed and disposed of in terms of the said judgment of this Court in Pushpa's case supra.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP as well as learned counsel for the respondents submit that there is no merit in the petition and that the same is liable to be dismissed.

6. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that under identical circumstances in relation to the very same notification and acquisition proceedings, this Court in Pushpa's case supra, held as under:-
"The petitioner has challenged an endorsement dated 08.01.2019 issued by the respondent No.2 refusing to entertain a reference under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (henceforth referred to as 'Act of 2013').
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 2.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The petitioner claims that her husband had purchased Sy.No.99/3 of Manvi Taluk,
Raichur District from the respondent No.4 in terms of a sale deed dated 06.04.2015.
The name of her husband was entered in the revenue records.
After his death, the name of the petitioner was entered in the revenue records.

The petitioner contends that a notification dated 16.06.2015 was issued by the respondent No.1 proposing to acquire property of the petitioner along with other properties for the purposes of formation of house sites.
The name of the respondent No.4 appeared in the notification as the occupant of the land.
The respondent No.2 thereafter passed an award determining the compensation at a sum of Rs.18,01,462/- and issued a notice of the award on 03.04.2017 to the respondent No.4.
The respondent No.2 found that though the name of the respondent No.4 was mentioned in the notification, the revenue records as on that date stood in the name of the petitioner.

The respondent No.3 therefore, initiated proceedings under Section 77(1) of the Act of 2013 before the I Additional District Judge, Raichur, in Misc.No.873/2018 to determine the person to whom the amount was payable.

In the said proceedings, the respondent No.3 filed a Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176140793/
3 memo on 19.11.2018 depositing the award amount of Rs.18,01,462/-.

entities.text: Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner contends that notice of Misc.No.873/2018 was served on her on 16.12.2018 and that she entered appearance and filed an application under Section 151 of CPC to release the amount deposited.
Likewise, the respondent No.4 appeared and also filed an application for release of the deposited amount.

The District Court after conducting a summary trial, allowed the NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 application filed by the petitioner and directed a sum of Rs.18,01,462/- to be released in favour of the petitioner.

The petitioner who came to know of the award passed by the respondent No.2 on 16.12.2018, filed an application before the respondent No.2 on 26.12.2018 under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 seeking proper adjudication and ascertaining correct market value of the land acquired in view of its non- agricultural potential.

This application was rejected by the respondent No.2 in terms of an endorsement dated 08.01.2019 on the ground that the petitioner did not seek for a reference within the time specified under Section 64 of the Act 2013.
3. Being aggrieved by the said endorsement, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was unaware of the acquisition and notice of the award was not issued to the petitioner but was issued to the respondent No.4.
Therefore, he contends that the time for seeking reference under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 did not commence until the petitioner was notified of the award.
He submits that the petitioner came to know of the award only on 16.12.2018 and hence, reference sought for under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 on 26.12.2018 is within time.
Even otherwise, he contends that the respondent No.2 is bound to condone the delay by considering the cause shown for the delay in seeking the reference.

He submits that a perusal of Section 64 shows that the respondent No.2 is invested with the necessary discretion to condone the delay NC:
2024:KHC-K:8329 and therefore, the respondent No.2 ought to have exercised jurisdiction to refer the case under Section 64 of the Act of 2013.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submits that the time prescribed under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 seeking for a reference is to compel the landlooser to seek for reference at the earliest possible as that would affect the economics of the project.
He therefore, submits that the respondent No.2 was justified in rejecting the request for reference under Section 64 of the Act of 2013.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
7. It is not in dispute that the husband of the petitioner had purchased the land in question from the respondent No.4.
It is also not in dispute that the name of the respondent No.4 was mentioned as an occupant in the notification issued by the respondent No.1 for acquisition of the land.

It is also not in dispute that the petitioner was not heard before passing the award and she did not participate in the Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176140793/
4 proceedings.

entities.text: Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also not in dispute that after the award was finalized, a notice of the award was issued to the respondent No.4 and not to the petitioner.

When the respondent No.2 was under a doubt as to who was entitled for the compensation, the respondent No.2 ought to have NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 resorted to the remedy provided under Section 77(2) of the Act of 2013 which reads as follows:-
"77. Payment of compensation or deposit of same in Authority.-

( 1 ) xxxxx (2) If the person entitled to compensation shall not consent to receive it, or if there be no person competent to alienate the land, or if there be any dispute as to the title to receive the compensation or as to the apportionment of it

, the Collector shall deposit the amount of the compensation in the Authority to which a reference under Section 64 would be submitted:
Provided that any person admitted to be interested may receive such payment under protest as to the sufficiency of the amount:
Provided further that no person who has received the amount otherwise than under protest shall be entitled to make any application under sub-section (1) of Section 64:

Provided also that nothing herein contained shall affect the liability of any person,
who may receive the whole or any part of any compensation awarded under this Act,
to pay the same to the person lawfully entitled thereto."

8. Once respondent No.3 deposits the award amount under Section 77(2) of the Act of 2013, then it is invariable that a reference under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 also would be submitted by respondent No.2.
In that event, the authority would have taken out the proceedings as provided under Section 64 of the Act of 2013.

However,
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 respondent No.2 did not resort to the remedy under Section 77(2) of the Act of 2013, but resorted to the procedure contemplated under Section 77(1) of the Act of 2013.
The petitioner has nowhere contended that she was aware of the award proceedings or that she participated in the award proceedings and that notice of the award was issued to her.

9. A perusal of Section 64 of the Act of 2013 shows that a person who was interested in the acquired land and who had not accepted the award may require the acquiring agency to refer to the authority any objections regarding measurement or the amount of the compensation or the person to whom it is payable.

In case the acquiring agency fails to refer the application to the authority within a period thirty days, the person affected is entitled to request the acquiring authority to make a reference to it within a period of thirty days thereafter.

If the person interested was present or represented before the acquiring agency when he made the award, then such reference shall be made within six weeks from the date of award and in other cases, within six weeks from the date of receipt of a notice of the award under Section 21 of the Act of 2013,
Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176140793/
5 or within six months from the date of collector's award, whichever expires first.

De hors this, the acquiring authority may entertain the application after the expiry of the said period, within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified.
10. In the case on hand, the award was passed on 31.03.2017 and the petitioner did not participate in the award nor did she receive a notice of the award under Section 12(2)
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894
. Therefore, the time for seeking a reference under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 did not commence insofar as the petitioner was concerned.

The time commenced only when she was served with the notice in Civil Miscellaneous No.873/2018 i.e., on 16.12.2018 and therefore, the application filed by the petitioner under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 was well within the time.

11. In that view of the matter, the endorsement issued by respondent No.2 rejecting the application filed by the petitioner seeking for reference under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 deserves to be interfered with.
Consequently, the petition is allowed.

The impugned endorsement issued by respondent No.2 dated 08.01.2019 is quashed and respondent No.2 is directed to refer the application of the petitioner to the authority within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

7. As can be seen from the aforesaid order, the 2nd respondent-SLAO of the Karnataka Housing Board having issued an Endorsement to the effect that the claim of the petitioner for reference to the authority for enhancement of compensation under Section 64 of the said Act of 2013 was quashed by this Court and the 2nd respondent - SLAO was directed to refer the application of the petitioner /
land owner to the authority.

It is a matter of record and an undisputed fact that the that the present petition also relates to the subject lands which arises out of the very same Notification - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 and the same acquisition proceedings and consequently, the present petition also deserves to be allowed and disposed of in terms of the aforesaid order.

8. At any rate, the material on record would also disclose that the petitioner was not served with notice of the award and consequently, the extendable / condonable period of limitation of one year under the second proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 64 of the said Act of 2013 would be applicable to the facts of the instant case and consequently, the period of limitation of one year as provided in the second proviso would expire only on 30.09.2018 and since the petitioner submitted a representation on 26.09.2018, within the aforesaid period of limitation which would expire 30.09.2018, I am of the considered opinion that the impugned Endorsement rejecting the request of the petitioner to refer the claim to the authority for re-determination is contrary to facts and law and Smt.Ningamma W/O Ayyappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176140793/
6 the same deserves to be quashed.

9. In the result, I pass the following:-
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:8329 ORDER (i) Petition is hereby allowed and disposed of in terms of the order passed by this Court in the case of Smt.Pushpa vs. State of Karnataka and others - W.P.No.216421/2020 dated 12.06.2024.

entities.text: Smt.Pushpa vs. State of Karnataka and others - W.P.No.216421/2020 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The impugned Endorsement at Annexure-C dated 26.12.2018 is hereby quashed.

(iii) The 2nd respondent - SLAO is directed to refer the application of the petitioner to the authority under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Sd/-
(S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR) JUDGE Srl.

7
